messages:
marie: Quick heads-up — I pushed a tiny sample app that demonstrates adaptive client-side QoS for the SDKs (JS + Py). It's in the devex/qos-samples repo. https://git.internal/redwood/devex/qos-samples :wave:

sam: Nice. Does it cover pagination + concurrency limits? Those are the two things our frontend folks keep tripping over.

marie: Yup — two endpoints: /stream (low-latency single stream) and /batch (paginated requests with concurrency cap). The readme explains the backoff strategy we used.

lee: Can you summarize the backoff? We've been seeing a 401 -> 429 retry loop if token refresh races with throttles.

marie: Good call. Strategy is: 1) token refresh is orthogonal: if you get 401, try refresh once and retry immediately; 2) if you get 429, apply token-bucket + exponential jittered backoff and reduce concurrency; 3) if 401 happens after a 429, don't retry refresh more than once per 30s for that session to avoid hammering auth.

sam: That 30s window is interesting. Any data behind it?

marie: We tested with a synthetic load profile. Metrics in the repo: refresh traffic spikes correlated with cascading 429s in ~70% of runs without the window. With it, error tail dropped ~40%.

alex: For parity: JS and Python clients both implement the same QoS primitives (tokenBucket, maxConcurrency, dynamicWindow). API shape is slightly different due to language idioms but behavior should match. If you find a gap, please open an issue and tag @devex.

lee: Where's the sample config? I want to try with our token rotation frequency.

marie: In repo: ./configs/adaptive-default.yaml. Example snippet: ```yaml
max_concurrency: 12
initial_bucket: 60
refill_rate_per_sec: 5
auth_refresh_cooldown_sec: 30
panic_threshold: 0.15  # frac of requests failing => drop concurrency by 30%
```

sam: Any gotchas for streaming vs paginated flows?

marie: Streaming keeps a small reserved pool so single-user low-latency streams aren't blocked. Paginated flows borrow from the shared pool and respect per-route quotas. That prevents a huge pagination job from starving streams.

lee: I'm worried about onboarding friction: we should expose a single config knob like `adaptive_mode: true` so customers don't need to tune dozens of fields.

alex: Agreed. We have an RFC branch that adds profiles: perf, cost-saver, conservative. The sample app shows how to switch profiles at runtime.

sam: Also need clear docs on auth+retry interplay. People expect 401 -> refresh -> immediate retry and 429 -> retry-with-backoff. But mixing them is messy.

marie: Added a short doc/diagram in the repo. I'll also add a tiny troubleshooting checklist: "sees 429 after refresh" -> check refresh cooldown config, check token TTL alignment, enable debug logs.

lee: One more DX bug I hit: the Python SDK was returning a generic RetryError for both 401 and 429, so you can't distinguish to decide refresh vs backoff.

alex: That's a bug. The SDK should surface error.code for HTTP-level reasons. @sam can you file a parity issue and mark high priority?

sam: Filed: https://git.internal/redwood/devex/issues/142 — added repro steps and stack traces.

ci-bot: CI: qos-samples tests passed on branch adaptive-client-qos (build #782). :white_check_mark:

marie: Sweet. Next steps: I'll add the single-knob profiles and a short cook-book for customers migrating from naive retry loops. If anyone wants to pair on the Python error shape fix, ping me. :coffee:

lee: I'll pair tomorrow morning. Thanks for the sample, marie — this will help reduce onboarding tickets. :raised_hands:
